Name: Trait and Clothing Compatibility Mod (TACC)
Description:
[h2]Traits and Clothing Compatibility[/h2]
One colonist sees a second-hand jacket and calls it a bargain. Another sees a reason to complain. Everyone has questions about the uniform that arrived with a previous owner's obituary.

Trait and Clothing Compatibility (TACC) gives your crew's wardrobe a second opinion. It automatically configures each colonist's clothing policy around their traits, using Stardeus's own equipment policies and replacement system.

[h2]Features[/h2]

[h3]A dress code with room for personality[/h3]
- Thrifty colonists may wear second-hand clothing by default.
- Fastidious colonists and other beings with mental health avoid second-hand clothing by default.
- Corpse-origin and tattered clothing are forbidden by default for those profiles.
- Minds without mental health receive no additional mood-based restrictions.

For TACC-managed colonists, eligible clothing is ranked by the complete outfit's mood result first. Thrifty colonists can prefer a second-hand bargain over new clothing; everyone still considers corpse-origin and tattered penalties. Equal-mood choices use the game's normal value-and-quality comparison.

[h3]You set the wardrobe rules[/h3]
Adjust Second-hand, Corpse-origin, and Tattered settings separately for each trait profile. Search the colonist list and opt individual beings out whenever you prefer to handle their clothes yourself.

A saved Allow forbidden loose equipment setting lets TACC-managed colonists consider compatible items carrying the red forbidden marker without clearing it or changing ordinary hauling.

TACC responds when colonists join or their traits change. Existing manual slots, item choices, colors, stricter quality requirements, and replacement settings are respected. Changing an individual policy outside TACC pauses its management for that being.

[h3]Wash away the worst part of the history[/h3]
Unlock the 2x2 Washing Machine with Storage research. When automatic washing is enabled, powered idle machines collect stored corpse-origin clothing through ordinary hauling jobs. You can also select one item or a mixed group and choose Wash manually.

A completed cycle replaces Taken from the dead with Second-hand while preserving quality. It works on worn-slot clothing such as hats, helmets, suits, and clothes. Weapons stay out of the laundry, where they belong.

The machine has three standard upgrade slots. Speed Upgrades shorten the cycle, while Energy Efficiency Upgrades reduce active power demand. Each module uses Core's normal 15% stacking behavior.

[h3]Familiar equipment behavior[/h3]
Clothing changes follow the game's normal equipment jobs. With Keep until replaced selected, an unsuitable outfit can remain worn until a suitable replacement is available. Native life-support safeguards still apply.

An empty automatic clothing slot becomes the managed colonist's highest-priority personal task. A completely naked colonist may interrupt ordinary work after the usual grace period when compatible clothing is waiting. Improvements to filled slots wait their turn.

TACC changes clothing provenance only through completed Washing Machine jobs. Core still owns mood formulas, eligibility filters, equipment jobs, trade pricing, and weapon choices. TACC changes only the final clothing comparison for managed worn slots, putting that wearer's total mood result first.

[h3]Known traits and a helpful paper trail[/h3]
The Traits & log tab shows the reviewed clothing effects for Thrifty, Fastidious, Optimist, Pessimist, and other traits. A scrolling diagnostic log reports unfamiliar traits, changed equipment effects, and detected compatibility changes.

Unknown findings remain unknown to TACC until a mod update includes a reviewed comparison. Clear diagnostic log checks again immediately, so an unresolved finding returns. Copy the log when you want to share the details.

Expanded Traits is optional. TACC recognizes the reviewed Expanded Traits catalog when that exact version is installed, including generated pet affinities, without reporting its traits as missing when the mod is absent.

This log is present for debugging purposes. A mod update may, or may not, be provided based on the contents of the log.

[h3]At home in your ship's interface[/h3]
Open TACC from its clothing button on the top bar. The Traits & log, Policies, and Colonists tabs follow the selected game theme. Settings and individual opt-outs are saved with the colony.

[h2]Requirements[/h2]
Requires Stardeus 0.15 and Auto Utilities Mod Framework 1.4.0, installed separately.

Your crew keeps its personality. Its wardrobe gets a little supervision.
